newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian March industrial output drops 11.66 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombian March industrial output drops 11.66 pct.

text.p: Colombia's industrial output, excluding coffee processing, plummeted by 11.66 percent in March compared with the same month last year, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said Friday.

The worse-than-expected slump in activity in the manufacturing sector underscored the depth of the recession the country slipped into in January-March, when it posted its second consecutive quarter of negative economic growth, analysts said.

It also added to one of the worst quarters on record in terms of industrial output, since DANE said overall production in January-March -- excluding coffee processing -- dropped by 6.94 percent from the first quarter of 1996.
Industrial output including coffee processing was off 5.40 percent in the first quarter compared to the same period last year, the Statistics Department said.
It said the coffee processing sector and the oil products and tobacco industries were the only parts of the manufacuring sector that showed signs of positive growth in the first quarter.

Employment in the sector dropped 5.75 percent from the levels obtained in the first quarter of 1996, adding to what the DANE had previously described as Colombia's worst urban unemployment rate in nearly a decade.

Industrial sales, excluding those by the coffee processing sector, fell by an average of 6.13 percent in the first quarter compared to the same period a year ago, although sales fell by more than 10 percent in many sub-sectors, DANE said.

Growth is widely expected to pick up slightly in the second half of 1997, fueled by growth in oil and coffee revenues. But many leading analysts say they see Colombia's 1997 gross domestic product expanding by no more than about 2.5 percent, one of the lowest growth rates of any major country in the region.
